text:
If you're hoping to dodge the raincoat today, temper those expectations a bit. Burlington's holding onto a few leftover showers this Thursday, high near 77 under mostly cloudy skies, and while NWS calls it a coin-flip fifty percent chance, the models are split on just how wet: the American model keeps it fairly light, but the Euro and especially the sharper American model are both leaning much soggier. I'd carry the rain jacket and not be shocked by a rumble of thunder this afternoon, though nothing that should ruin your day. On the water, north winds 5 to 15 knots and waves a foot or less, with a shower or stray thunderstorm possible into the evening, so keep an eye on the sky if you're out on the broad lake.

The good news is Friday looks like the reward for today's patience, mostly sunny, high near 82, light winds, and a genuinely calm lake for anyone wanting a proper evening on the water. Enjoy that one, because the forecasters are already watching a wetter, unsettled Sunday build in behind it. For today, plan your outdoor errands for whenever the sky looks brightest, and I wouldn't schedule anything lake-side after mid-afternoon without a backup plan.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST: BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Happy Thursday! We continue to hang on to a few leftover showers into this Thursday. The showers will become lighter and more scattered in nature this afternoon. Most of us will only look at another few tenths of an inch of rain through the day ahead. High temperatures for the day climb back into the low and mid-70s for this afternoon. We are left mainly dry tonight, but there could be a spot shower or two, as lows fall back into upper 50s and lower 60s for most.
